speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the history. To better understand your neck and arm pain, paresthesias, and muscle weakness, can you tell me if these symptoms worsen when you tilt your head to one side or extend your neck?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: That helps narrow the differential; does the pain radiate down into your fingers, and do you notice any numbness in your thumb or middle finger? Additionally, have you experienced any issues with balance or coordination since the accident?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Burning pain in neck and arms, and weakness in both hands. I also have Paresthesias in hands, Absent reflexes, Decreased hand grip with fasciculations.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS) with concomitant Cervical Spondylotic Myelopathy.

REQUEST TEST: EMG/Nerve Conduction Study, Cervical MRI.
